# Visualising Geospatial Point Data

## 1. Overview

Proportional symbol maps (also known as graduate symbol maps) are a class of maps that use the visual variable of size to represent differences in the magnitude of a discrete, abruptly changing phenomenon, e.g. counts of people. Like choropleth maps, you can create classed or unclassed versions of these maps. The classed ones are known as range-graded or graduated symbols, and the unclassed are called proportional symbols, where the area of the symbols are proportional to the values of the attribute being mapped. In this hands-on exercisem we will learn how to create a proportional symbol map showing the number of wins by Singapore Pools' outlets using R package called **tmap**.

### 1.1 Learning Outcome

By the end of this hands-on exercise, we will acquire the following skills by using appropriate R packages:

- Import an aspatial data file into R
- Convert it into simple point feature data frame and at the same time, assign an appropriate projection reference to the newly created simple point feature data frame
- Plot interactive proportional symbol maps

## 2. Getting Started

Before we get started, we need to ensure that **tmap** package of R and other related R packages have been installed and loaded into R.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
pacman::p_load(sf, tmap, tidyverse)
```

## 3. Geospatial Data Wrangling

### 3.1 The Data

The data set used for this hands-on exercise is called *SGPools_svy21*. The data is in csv file format.

Figure below shows the first 15 records of SGPools_svy21.csv. It consists of seven columns. THe XCOORD and YCOORD columns are the x-coordinates and y-coordinates of SingPools outlets and branches. They are in [Singapore SVY21 Projected Coordinates System](https://app.sla.gov.sg/sirent/About/PlaneCoordinateSystem).

![](data/SGPools.jpg)

### 3.2 Data Import and Preparation

The code chunk below uses *read_csv()* function of **readr** package to import *SGPools_svy21.csv* into R as a tibble data frame called *sgpools*.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
sgpools <- read_csv("data/SGPools_svy21.csv")
```

After importing the data file into R, it is important for us to examine if the data file has been imported correctly.

The code chunk below shows *list()* is used to do the job.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
list(sgpools) 
```

Notice that the *sgpools* data is in tibble data frame and not the common R data frame.

### 3.3 Creating a *sf* data frame from an aspatial data frame

The code chunk below conversts sgpools data frame into a simple feature data frame by using *st_as_sf()* of **sf** packages.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
sgpools_sf <- st_as_sf(sgpools, 
                       coords = c("XCOORD", "YCOORD"),
                       crs= 3414)
```

::: callout-note
## Things to learn from the code chunk above

- The *coords* argument requires you to provide the column name of the x-coordinates first then followed by the column name of the y-coordinates.
- The *crs* argument required you to provide the coordinates system in epsg format. [EPSG: 3414](https://epsg.io/3414) is Singapore SVY21 Projected Coordinate System. We can search for other country's epsg code by referring to [epsg.io](https://epsg.io/).
:::

Figure below shows the data table of *sgpools_sf*. Notice that a new column called *geometry* has been added into the data frame.

![](data/SGPools3.jpg) We can also display the basic information of the newly created *sgpools_sf* by using the code chunk below:

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
list(sgpools_sf) 
```

The output shows that *sgpools_sf* is in point feature class. Its epsg ID is 3414. The bbox provide information of the extend of the geospatial data.

## 4. Drawing Proportional Symbol Map

To create an interactive proportional symbol map in R, the *view* mode of **tmap** will be used.

The code chunk below will turn on the interactive mode of **tmap**.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
tmap_mode("view")
```

::: panel-tabset
### An interactive Point Symbol Map

```{r}
#| label: interactive_point_symbol_map
#| code-fold: true
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6
#| warning: false

tm_shape(sgpools_sf) + 
  tm_bubbles(fill = "red",
           size = 1,
           col = "black",
           lwd = 1)
```

### Make it Proportional

To draw a proportional symbol map, we need to assign a numerical variable to the size visual attribute. The code chunks below shows that the variable *Gp1Gp2Winnings* is assigned to size visual attribute.

```{r}
#| label: interactive_point_symbol_map_Proportional
#| code-fold: true
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6
#| warning: false

tm_shape(sgpools_sf) + 
  tm_bubbles(fill = "red",
             size = "Gp1Gp2 Winnings",
             col = "black",
             lwd = 1)
```

### Give it a Different Colour

The proportional symbol map can be further improved by using the colour visual attribute. In the code chunk below, *OUTLET_TYPE* variable is used as the colour attribute variable.

```{r}
#| label: interactive_point_symbol_map_different_Colour
#| code-fold: true
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6
#| warning: false

tm_shape(sgpools_sf) + 
  tm_bubbles(fill = "OUTLET TYPE", 
             size = "Gp1Gp2 Winnings",
             col = "black",
             lwd = 1)
```

### Twin Diagrams

An impressive and little-know feature of **tmap**'s view mode is that it also works with faceted plots. The argument *sync* in *tm_facets()* can be used in this case to produce multiple maps with synchronised zoom and pan settings.

```{r}
#| label: interactive_point_symbol_map_twin_diagrams
#| code-fold: true
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4
#| warning: false

tm_shape(sgpools_sf) + 
  tm_bubbles(fill = "OUTLET TYPE", 
             size = "Gp1Gp2 Winnings",
             col = "black",
             lwd = 1) + 
  tm_facets(by= "OUTLET TYPE",
            nrow = 1,
            sync = TRUE)
```
:::

## 5. Ending the Session

Before we end this session, it is wiser to switch **tmap**'s Viewer back to plot mode by using the code chunk below.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
tmap_mode("plot")
```
